summary: The non_gaia variant is code-only. It implements a simple simulated pipeline for sensor generation, coordination, hotspot analysis, alerting, and room notifications, but it repeatedly models rats rather than the requested cockroach-monitoring domain and leaves the declared CrewAI orchestration empty. The result is partially aligned with the requirements but needs revision before it can be considered a faithful system design.

findings.description: The variant includes a sensor-to-coordinator-to-alert pipeline and stores count, location, and timestamp fields.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/sensor_agent.py:6-10 defines SensorData with sensor_id, location, timestamp, rat_count; lines 18-28 generate sensor data; non_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:42-63 processes that data through coordinator, alerting, and notification agents.

findings.description: The coordinator analyzes collected readings and identifies high-activity locations using aggregate statistics.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/coordinator_agent.py:26-56 implements analyze_patterns() and identify_hotspots(); non_gaia/implementation_workspace/utils/analysis.py:6-44 provides similar analysis and hotspot helper functions.

findings.description: The code consistently models a rat detection system instead of the required cockroach infestation system, including class names, field names, printed output, and analysis keys.
findings.evidence: requirements.json requires identifying cockroach presence; non_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:12 defines RatDetectionSystem; non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/sensor_agent.py:10 and utils/data_models.py:10 use rat_count; main.py:67 prints Starting Rat Detection and Alerting System.

findings.description: The declared CrewAI orchestration is not actually specified: the crew has no tasks, and the runtime flow uses direct method calls instead of agent communication contracts.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:23-28 creates Crew(... tasks=[] ...); main.py:35-63 directly calls sensor.generate_data(), coordinator.receive_data(), alerting.send_alert(), and notification.update_room_status().

findings.description: The alerting and notification behavior is simulated with hardcoded contacts and print statements rather than actual delivery interfaces.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/alerting_agent.py:7-10 hardcodes contact lists; lines 12-31 print and dispatch to private mock methods; notification_agent.py:14-27 prints notification data.

findings.description: The sensor behavior is random simulation and does not model motion-sensor input or a regular autonomous send loop from each device to a central agent.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/sensor_agent.py:18-28 generates random counts; non_gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:72-82 runs five fixed simulation periods.

logical_inconsistencies: The requirements describe cockroach monitoring, but the implementation names and data model describe rats throughout.
The code imports and constructs CrewAI concepts, but the actual system behavior bypasses CrewAI tasks and agent communication.
implementation_risks: A domain mismatch could invalidate downstream alerts, reports, and stakeholder expectations.
Empty CrewAI task configuration means the apparent multi-agent framework does not execute a defined agent workflow.
Hardcoded mock contacts and print-based delivery cannot satisfy real administrative, student, or pest-control notification needs.
